introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A function $f$ is defined by $f: x \mapsto \dfrac{2x+1}{x-4},\ x \in \mathbb{R},\ x \neq 4$.

(a) Show that $f$ is injective.

(b) Find the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$, stating its domain. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)** A function is injective (one-to-one) if $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$ implies $x_1 = x_2$. Write $f(x) = \dfrac{2x+1}{x-4} = 2 + \dfrac{9}{x-4}$, since $2(x-4) + 9 = 2x + 1$.

Suppose $x_1, x_2 \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\{4\}$ with $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$. Then

$$2 + \frac{9}{x_1 - 4} = 2 + \frac{9}{x_2 - 4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{9}{x_1 - 4} = \frac{9}{x_2 - 4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1 - 4 = x_2 - 4 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1 = x_2.$$

Hence $f$ is injective. (Equivalently, $f'(x) = -\dfrac{9}{(x-4)^2} < 0$ for all $x \neq 4$, so $f$ is strictly decreasing on each branch, and the branch $x < 4$ takes only values less than $2$ while the branch $x > 4$ takes only values greater than $2$, so no value is repeated.)

**(b)** Let $y = \dfrac{2x+1}{x-4}$ and make $x$ the subject:

$$y(x - 4) = 2x + 1 \ \Longrightarrow\ xy - 4y = 2x + 1 \ \Longrightarrow\ x(y - 2) = 4y + 1 \ \Longrightarrow\ x = \frac{4y + 1}{y - 2}.$$

Exchanging the names of the variables:

$$\boxed{f^{-1}(x) = \frac{4x + 1}{x - 2}}$$

The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$. Since $f(x) = 2 + \dfrac{9}{x-4}$ and $\dfrac{9}{x-4}$ takes every real value except $0$, the range of $f$ is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{2\}$. Hence

$$\boxed{\text{domain of } f^{-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R} : x \neq 2\}}$$

(this agrees with the denominator $x - 2$ of $f^{-1}$ vanishing at $x = 2$).

questions.enonce_markdown: A relation $R$ is defined on the set of integers by: $a R b \iff a + b = 2m + 1$, where $m$ is an integer. Show that $R$ is not an equivalence relation. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A relation is an equivalence relation only if it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. It is enough to show that one of these properties fails.

$a R b$ means that $a + b = 2m + 1$ for some integer $m$, that is, **$a + b$ is odd**.

**Not reflexive.** Take any integer $a$, for example $a = 1$. Then $a + a = 2a = 2$, which is even, so it cannot equal $2m + 1$ for an integer $m$ (it would give $m = \tfrac12$). So $1\,R\,1$ is false (and $a R a$ fails for every integer $a$ because $2a$ is always even).

Hence $R$ is not reflexive, and therefore $R$ is not an equivalence relation.

*Remark.* $R$ is symmetric ($a + b = b + a$), but it is also not transitive: $1\,R\,2$ (since $1 + 2 = 3$ is odd) and $2\,R\,3$ (since $2 + 3 = 5$ is odd), yet $1 + 3 = 4$ is even, so $1\,R\,3$ is false.
